rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the jihad directive, the hypocrites displayed zeal and sincerity; once commanded, they feared people more than God and hid themselves.
rows.anchor: once this directive was given, they began fearing people more than God and went about hiding themselves.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression rendered as fa-awlā conveys a curse and hatred, equivalent in meaning to waylun lahum.
rows.anchor: express curse and hate. They have the same meaning as

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should have welcomed the jihad directive with the customary pledge to hear and obey, then proved their promise to God through action.
rows.anchor: right attitude for them was to welcome this directive of jihād by the conventional words “we have listened and we obeyed,”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ṭāʿatun wa-qawlun maʿrūf is a fronted subject with its predicate omitted for contextual emphasis and eloquence.
rows.anchor: are in the place of mubtadā’ and the khabar is suppressed because of strong contextual indication and as a requisite of eloquence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawlun maʿrūf refers to “we heard and obeyed,” the customary response of God's sincere servants to every command.
rows.anchor: It is this expression which is what is conventional and customary for God from His sincere people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-idhā indicates that a matter has been settled and a practical measure is about to be undertaken.
rows.anchor: the matter has been decided, and that it has been resolved to undertake some practical measure for it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once God and the Prophet communicated the final decision to launch jihad, the hypocrites should have made their verbal pledge real in practice.
rows.anchor: when the final decision to launch it was communicated to them by God and His Prophet (sws), they should have substantiated their words through practice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier directive in verse 4 called for preparation and encouragement, while the practical step to launch jihad came later.
rows.anchor: The practical step to launch it came later.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prior service to the Messenger had been mere claims; proving commitment now would open much good, but they chose cowardice.
rows.anchor: till now whatever they have done for the Messenger of God is merely making claims. The time to test this claim has just come.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from speaking about hypocrites to addressing them directly intensifies the exhortation.
rows.anchor: in this verse, they are directly addressed. This change in style is meant to reinforce the exhortation done to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they turn away from the message, they will neither benefit themselves nor their nation and will spread social disorder and sever kinship, as in jāhiliyyah.
rows.anchor: they will not be able to benefit themselves or give any to their nation and end up in spreading anarchy in the society and severing blood relationships

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group of hypocrites sought compromise with Quraysh and the Jews, promising continued loyalty in some matters; war exposed their inability to fight alongside Muslims.
rows.anchor: among them was one group which wanted to strike a compromise with the disbelievers of the Quraysh.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The compromisers promoted peace rhetoric to conceal their hypocrisy, but their chosen policy returned society to anarchy and the killing of fellow humans.
rows.anchor: the path they have adopted for themselves and the path they want others to adopt as well is not the path of peace and reconciliation; it is like turning back to anarchy and killing one’s fellow human beings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True peace and brotherhood require serving one God and recognizing humanity's descent from Adam; this is the Qur'an's call and Islam's collective foundation.
rows.anchor: The path of peace and brotherhood is that all should lead their lives as servants of one God and as the descendents of one Adam

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's curse leaves them deaf and blind to truth: despite recognizing divine light, they turn back to jāhiliyyah and lose that light.
rows.anchor: their ears have lost the ability to hear the truth and their eyes have lost the real vision to see the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an revives hearts when people reflect on it; their refusal to ponder lets rust close their hearts like locks.
rows.anchor: the rust which comes on hearts has in fact inflicted their hearts; so just as locks close doors, their hearts too have been closed because of this rust.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite noun qulub expresses abhorrence; similarly, the indefinite wajuhan in 4:47 conveys hatred, as if the hearts are too hateful to identify.
rows.anchor: so horrible and hateful are these hearts that the speaker does not even want to refer to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heart maladies include love of life, fear of death, stinginess, cowardice, jealousy, and hypocrisy; political power can add arrogance and hard-heartedness.
rows.anchor: Love of life, fear of death, stinginess, cowardice, jealousy, hypocrisy and other similar things are some of their prominent components.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Listening to and understanding the Qur'an cures these maladies, but those who evade and dread it cannot be treated.
rows.anchor: The remedy to these maladies is to listen and to understand the Qur’ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites' conduct resembles apostasy: they knew the Prophet's call was true, accepted it, then let Satan mislead them when trials came, while God gave respite.
rows.anchor: The attitude of these hypocrites is akin to apostasy. They fully knew that what the Prophet (sws) was calling them to is the path of truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrisy is tantamount to apostasy, as 5:54 describes believers who renounce faith being replaced by people loved by God and loving Him.
rows.anchor: It is evident from other places of the Qur’ ān also that hypocrisy is tantamount to apostasy.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb's subject is God, not Satan; the Qur'anic verb is used for God alone, and Yusuf 12:110 provides another example of contextual identification.
rows.anchor: The subject of the verb H is God. In the Qur’ān, this verb is used for Him only

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite knowing the truth, hypocrites connived with Quraysh and Jewish leaders who opposed revelation, promising to side with them in hard times.
rows.anchor: These hypocrites assured them that in some matters they will keep siding with them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same hypocrites promised Jews they would leave with them if expelled, as reported in 59:11; God's knowledge of their secret collusion is a threat and warning.
rows.anchor: this sentence is not merely a piece of information; it reflects threat and warning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment begins when stern angels take their souls, striking their mouths and backs, with no one able to help.
rows.anchor: The punishment of those who conspire against Islam begins right from the time angels claim their souls

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They meet this fate because they pursued what displeased God and avoided what pleased Him; angels torment them from death and God nullifies their apparently pious deeds.
rows.anchor: God will lay waste all their seemingly pious deeds they did while claiming to be adherents of Islam.
